text.p: Here are highlights of stories in Romania's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
Business:
BURSA
- The new bank Banca de Credit Popular SA plans to issue 500,000 shares worth 50,000 lei each to set up its capital.
- The Dac Air private airline plans to publicly sell a 20 percent stake. Selling price is seen at around $10 per share.
ADEVARUL

- An IMF mission in Romania last week surveyed the real state of the economy. A statement from President Emil Constantinescu showed the economic situation had deteriorated and central bank governor Mugur Isarescu said time was working against Romania. "Any delay will cost us," he said.
- Performance of animal breeding farms can increase only after privatisation, a farm manager says.
AZI

- Faster privatisation of tourism companies is needed and aspects of the foreign investment law, including the right to own land, should be clarified, new Tourism Minister Akos Birtalan says in an interview.
ZIUA
- The agenda of today's meeting of the new government includes a decree on state budget allocations for people affected by landslides near the eastern city of Iasi.
LIBERTATEA
- The National Oil Company board is expected to discuss possible petrol price rises on Monday.
- Steel smelter Sidex SA plans to launch a $100 million bond issue in the international market to raise money needed for re-equipment, newspaper says.
CRONICA ROMANA
- The talks between the Romanian government and the International Monetary Fund emphasised the need for urgent reform measures.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- The new government plans to include the State Ownership Fund in its structure. In this way, the executive will become the owner and administrator of public property.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- The over-the-counter market expects 471 new listings this week. It now lists 1,026 stocks.
General:
ROMANIA LIBERA
- Hungarian border guards seized 700 kilos of hashish smuggled in a truck with Dutch number plates coming from Romania.
- National Peasant Party senator George Pruteanu calls for a parliament extraordinary session in January to discuss urgent laws for Romania's economy.
- Foreign Minister Adrian Severin will make an official visit to Hungary on December 27 following the ratification of a political treaty between the two countries.
EVENIMENTUL ZILEI
- MPs should give up the winter recess -- due until the early February -- and start work on vital laws, the newspaper editorial says.
- President Emil Constantinescu pledged to fight organised crime at the end of the European Union summit in Dublin.
- Austrian Herbert Stein is charged with alleged tax evasion worth tens of thousands of dollars after selling 100 cars and paying no import duties in Romania.
ADEVARUL

- The Hungarian Democratic Union (UDMR) -- the junior member of the centrist ruling coalition -- will get the prefect jobs in three of Romania's 42 counties, while the Social Democratic Union will get 12 such positions. The rest are held by the Democratic Convention.
- Romania stands equal chances to become a NATO member as Hungary, Poland, the Czech Republic and Slovenia, the newspaper says.
- French President Jacques Chirac reiterated his country's support for Romania's integration into the NATO.
- The western city of Timisoara hosts week-long ceremonies commemorating the beginning of the bloody 1989 revolution which ousted former Stalinist dictator Nicolae Ceausescu.
- Enthusiasm for celebrations of the revolution has died with the hardships of transition and falling living standards, the newspaper says.
CURIERUL NATIONAL
- Constantinescu called for the liberalisation of visas needed for Romanians to travel into Western European countries during the European Union summit in Dublin.
- European foreign ministers praised Romania for including the UDMR in its ruling coalition.
LIBERTATEA
- Some 45 percent of Romanians buy new products as an effect of advertising, newspaper says quoting a study by the Austrian marketing research institute Fessel+GfK.
- Bucharest police caught 95 drug smugglers in 1996, 41 of which were Iranian citizens and 20 Romanians. The police seized some 50 kilos of drugs, the newspaper says.
CRONICA ROMANA
- Constantinescu will attend ceremonies in Timisoara seven years after the start of the 1989 revolution.
VOCEA ROMANIEI
- The rate of tuberculosis among children of up to 14 years of age rose to 20 per hundred of thousand.
ZIUA
- Landslides in the eastern village of Parcovaci destroyed some 100 households. ($=3,768 lei) -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
